candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy shows CD1a+/S100+ mononuclear cells with reniform nuclei consistent with Langerhans cells, and there is multifocal disease (nail + scalp). Onychomatricoma has none of these features.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Onychomatricoma is a benign fibroepithelial tumor of the nail matrix; does not match the histologic, immunohistochemical, or multisystem findings

candidate_relations.reason: Although melanoma can be S100+, it is CD1a-negative and would not explain the scalp seborrheic-dermatitis-like lesions with identical histology, nor the subungual hemorrhages in multiple nails. The reniform nuclei and CD1a positivity are hallmarks of Langerhans cells, not melanocytes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Malignant melanoma would be CD1a-negative and typically S100+/HMB-45+/Melan-A+; does not fit the full clinicopathologic picture

candidate_relations.reason: Keratoacanthoma shows squamous differentiation and is CD1a-negative/S100-negative. It would not account for the scalp lesions or the diffuse infiltrate of reniform mononuclear cells.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Subungual keratoacanthoma is a squamoproliferative lesion; entirely inconsistent with the immunophenotype and multisystem presentation

case_quality_flags: All three candidates are clearly not equivalent to Langerhans cell histiocytosis; no partial or conflicting matches present in the registry.
